mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which is likely to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and encouraging investment.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows after UNRATE exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) remains high, it indicates inefficiencies in the labor market, potentially leading to economic stagnation and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 60-day windows despite the labor market inefficiency signal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion signals a potential economic slowdown, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following an INDPRO decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong demand in the housing market, which may boost related industries and lead to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following high HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) may lead to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 5-day windows after CPIAUCSL exceeds 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong but federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising, it may indicate inflation concerns, leading to negative equity returns as higher rates reduce consumer and business spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows despite the conflicting signals, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) in a late-cycle expansion may indicate a tight labor market, potentially leading to wage inflation and decreased corporate margins, resulting in negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE in a late-cycle expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.
